Chapter 7: Using Technology as an Accelerator, Not a Catalyst.
You know, in the journey to greatness, it’s tempting to see technology as a kind of magic bullet—something that lets you leap past competitors or change everything overnight. But here’s the thing: truly great organizations realize technology isn’t what makes them great in the first place. Instead, it’s a powerful tool that, when used wisely, can help them move faster down the path they’re already on.
Picture technology as the wind behind a ship’s sails. If you’ve got a ship that’s well-built, pointed in the right direction, and a crew that’s rowing together, that wind’s going to help you pick up speed. But if your ship’s falling apart or you’re drifting with no direction, even the strongest wind won’t take you where you want to go.
The best organizations approach technology with real discipline. They don’t just chase every new trend or grab onto the latest shiny gadget just to keep up. Instead, they ask: does this technology fit with what we do best? Can it actually help us reach our goals more effectively?
Here are a few practical ways to make technology work for you:
First, look for technology that fits your organization’s “sweet spot”—that place where your greatest strengths, your deepest passions, and your economic engine all come together.
Next, don’t get distracted by fads. If a hot new tool doesn’t help with your core priorities, it’s probably not worth your time.
Use technology to support, not replace, disciplined processes and genuine human judgment. And finally, only invest in tech when it gives you a real, lasting advantage—not just a temporary boost.
Take a company that’s already great at customer service. If they invest in a new customer relationship management system, they’re building on their strengths—deepening relationships and improving efficiency. But they’d skip out on flashy tech that doesn’t align with their mission or values.
When you treat technology as an accelerator, not a catalyst, you make sure every investment is purposeful and tied to your long-term strategy. That keeps you from wasting resources and helps you stay laser-focused on what truly matters.
So, with technology supporting your disciplined execution, the real question becomes: how do you build and sustain momentum over time? Let’s dive into that next.
